lemma: STAGE 1 TARGET (exploration; verbatim McKay-Murray-Williams STOC 2019 Thm 1.3, local mmw19/paper.txt l.115-118): if there is some time-constructible s(n) >= n and an A in PH such that search-MCSP^A[s(n)] is not solvable by a poly(s(n))-space streaming algorithm with poly(s(n)) update time, then P != NP. Streaming algorithms need not read a fresh bit each step. A decision lower bound for the same MCSP^A suffices a fortiori.

proved_step: STAGE 2 LEMMA (space ceiling; Lemma FB2 of research/PNP-001/lab/feedback-complexity/FEEDBACK-NOTE-2026-11-20.md, proof written out there): for MCSP[s] (and search-MCSP[s]) on truth tables of length N = 2^n read in one pass, there is a one-pass algorithm with O(s log(n+s)) = O(s log s) bits of memory (s >= n): keep the lexicographically first size-<=s circuit consistent with the prefix read so far; on a disagreeing bit search the next consistent circuit (unbounded update time). Conversely the number of Myhill-Nerode classes of prefixes is <= 1 + 2^{O(s log(n+s))}. Hence every pure space / communication argument ends at this value, which lies inside poly(s): only an UPDATE-TIME lower bound can establish the Stage 1 target.

Review: argument checked by cases. Suppose a correct total algorithm gives the same memory state after prefixes p1 != p2 of length t. Its later output depends only on the state and the continuation q, so it is equal for p1q and p2q. Case live p1, live p2 (distinct): choose q with p1q in SC_s. The output is a circuit C for p1q. Then C is the output for p2q: if p2q in SC_s, C must compute the different table p2q (distinct prefixes give distinct tables), contradiction; if p2q not in SC_s, the output must be bottom, not C, contradiction. Case live p, dead p' with p q in SC_s: output for pq is a circuit C, but for p'q (not in SC_s, since p' is dead) the output must be bottom, contradiction. The case analysis is exhaustive. Scope: deterministic total algorithm, non-uniform allowed, any encoding of the state. No gap found.

Review: the state is S bits, so an affine state map from F2^t to F2^S has fibres that are cosets of a kernel of dimension >= t-S. For t > S every fibre has size >= 2. Since SC_s is nonempty, some fibre contains a live prefix. By Satz B (S0010) a class containing a live prefix contains no other live prefix and no dead prefix, so it is a singleton. A coset of size >= 2 cannot be a singleton, contradiction. Hence no correct total algorithm has an affine state partition for t > S. Scope: affine partition of the prefix trie only. Not a hardness statement, as the spec says; it does not rule out non-affine updates (Berlekamp-Massey-type). No gap found. This step is elementary and does not close G0001, G0003 or G0004.

Review by a different session. Argument: an algorithm with memory S, update circuits F_t of size u_t (fan-in 2, inputs S+1) and decoder of size D is determined by these circuits. The number of fan-in-2 circuits of size u over S+1 inputs is at most 2^{O(u log(u+S))}, and the decoder count is 2^{O(D log D)}. Summing over t gives the stated bound on the number of computed functions, since the map configuration -> computed function is a function. Non-uniform constants are counted in the configuration. Scope exactly as the spec: relativises, any encoding, says nothing about succinctly described M_s. No gap found.

Review by a different session. The arithmetic is correct: reading all S/w words, computing F_t for free and writing back costs O(S/w) probes, so any S-bit algorithm has cell-probe update cost O(S/w) under free computation. Scope caveat (not a refutation): this is a probe count in a free-computation model; it does not bound the gate count u_t, which is the Lambda_S cost measure, so Lemma 2 gives no bound on sum_t CC(F_t). The phrase 'information-transfer arguments cannot exceed this' holds only conditionally on the existence of an S-bit algorithm (a lower bound above a valid achievable upper bound would contradict it). It does not close G0001, G0003 or G0004.

proved_step: LEMMA (affine updates, F_2 or any finite field): a one-pass total algorithm for Search-MCSP[s] (N = 2^n, SC_s nonempty) whose update z_{t+1} = M_t z_t + u_t b + c_t is affine in (state, bit) must use S >= N state bits. Proof: the state map p -> z(p) on {0,1}^t is affine, so its fibres are cosets of kernels of dimension >= t - S, hence of size >= 2 when t > S. A live prefix p (a prefix of some T in SC_s) has a second prefix p' in its fibre. By Satz B (S0010), p' is neither live nor dead-sharing, a contradiction, so S+1 > N. Scope: affine updates only, non-uniform allowed, a space statement (not update time), relativising; non-affine updates such as Berlekamp-Massey style are not covered.

proved_step: LEMMA L-F3 (repair of S0021 for p=3, linear and affine). Let A in F_3^{k x t}, c in F_3^k, and let phi(p) = A p + c on {0,1}^t. Then phi is injective on {0,1}^t iff rank_{F_3}(A) = t. PROOF. (a) If rank A < t, pick v != 0 with Av = 0. Each entry v_i lies in {0,1,2} = {0,1,-1} mod 3; let v' in {-1,0,1}^t be its representative, v' = p - q with p = max(v',0), q = max(-v',0) in {0,1}^t, p != q. Then phi(p) - phi(q) = A(p-q) = Av' = Av = 0 mod 3, so phi(p) = phi(q): collision. (b) If p != q in {0,1}^t with phi(p) = phi(q), then v = p - q in {-1,0,1}^t is nonzero and Av = 0 mod 3 (the constant c cancels), so rank A < t. Hence injective iff full column rank. SCOPE: p = 3 only. For p >= 5 only the implication (full rank => injective) holds. EXHAUSTIVE CHECK cm-ec5f0b8d2dc547ad: t=2,3, all linear matrices, 0 mismatches; random t=4,5, 0 mismatches. WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE: fibres of phi are not cosets, so the F_2 coset bound of S0021 does not transfer; no size or update-time bound follows; G0004 (update time) and G0003 remain open. This is a CLAIMED step, not reviewed.

lemma: Full-family necessity (any field F): if a machine stores state phi(p) = A p + c for prefix p in {0,1}^t and must output f(p) for every Boolean f on {0,1}^t, then phi is injective on {0,1}^t, i.e. ker A meets D_t = {p - q : p, q in {0,1}^t} only in 0. Proof: if phi(p) = phi(q) with p != q, take f with f(p)=1, f(q)=0; the output is a function of the state, so it cannot equal both. Also phi(p)-phi(q) = A(p-q). Scope: F arbitrary, affine phi, all Boolean targets. Over F_2 this is ker A meets {0,1}^t only in 0; over F_3 it is full column rank.

lemma: Pivot bound (any field F, any k, t). Let A in F^{k x t} have rank r and y in F^k. Then |{x in {0,1}^t : Ax = y}| <= 2^(t-r). Hence for phi(x)=Ax+c, every fibre meets {0,1}^t in at most 2^(t-r) points and |phi({0,1}^t)| >= 2^r. Proof: choose J, |J|=r, with A_J linearly independent columns; F = complement of J. For x in a fibre, A_J x_J = y - c - A_F x_F, so x_J is determined by x_F (full column rank). Hence x -> x_F is injective on the fibre, giving at most 2^(t-r) points; fibres partition {0,1}^t. Scope: upper bound on fibre size, does NOT give the fibres>=2 claim of G0006 (which stays refuted), and gives no update-time bound for G0004. Bookkeeping-level, recorded as LEMMA (not proved_step).

Let p be prime, A in F_p^{k x t} with rank r, c in F_p^k, phi(x) = Ax + c, B = {0,1}^t, D_t = {a - b : a, b in B} inside F_p^t, K(A) = |ker A intersect D_t|. Proof: (i) fix x0 in F intersect B; the map x -> x - x0 sends F intersect B injectively into ker A intersect D_t, and |ker A| = p^(t-r). lemma: BOOKKEEPING BOUND (exact, finite-scope-free). Let F be any set of truth tables on N = 2^n points and fix a prefix length k. For a prefix p of length k, its residual is R_p = {q : pq in F}. Then the number of distinct residual classes at level k is at most min(2^k, |F|) + 1. Proof: only prefixes that occur as the k-prefix of some f in F have nonempty residual, and there are at most min(2^k, |F|) of them. All other prefixes share the single empty residual, which adds at most one class.
gap: G0003 (update time) and G0004 (transition cost) remain open. The bound above is trivial and closes neither. It is a size bound on the state count, not a transition rule. Obstacle: a transition function on residual classes needs a fixed representation of a residual and a gate-cost model, and neither is defined yet.

lemma: IDENTIFICATION (exact, finite F). Let F be a set of N=2^n truth tables and fix the variable order x_0<...<x_{N-1} (bit x of a table). For k <= N, the number of distinct residual classes at level k, where the residual of a k-prefix p is R_p = {q : pq in F} and the empty residual is counted once, equals the width at level k of the minimal OBDD of the indicator of F in this order. Proof: a k-prefix p determines the subfunction f|_{x_<k = p} on the remaining variables, and R_p determines that subfunction and conversely; the empty residual is the constant-0 subfunction. Minimal OBDD width at a level is the number of distinct subfunctions (Bryant/Myhill-Nerode), so the claim is standard. Consequence: sum_k classes_k is the minimal OBDD size of F for the truth-table order, and the prefix automaton of EXT is this OBDD.
gap: G0003 and G0004 stay open. The identification gives no transition rule and no update-time bound; it only names the state count as an OBDD width. The trivial bound min(2^k,|F|)+1 is nearly tight at small k (classes = 2^k for k<=4 at n=4), so the non-trivial content lies in the middle levels. Measured maxima over displayed levels: n=3 gives 15, 21, 11 for s=1,2,3 (not monotone in s, since F grows while residual classes can merge); n=4 gives 39, 165, 489 for s=1,2,3 (levels k>=15 truncated in output).

lemma: SHARP COUNTING (any field F, any k, t). For phi(x)=Ax+c on {0,1}^t, D_t = {x-y : x,y in {0,1}^t} subset F^t. Claim: every fibre F_y of phi satisfies |F_y cap {0,1}^t| <= |ker A cap D_t|, hence 2^t <= |im phi| * |ker A cap D_t|. Proof: if F_y cap {0,1}^t is empty the claim is trivial. Otherwise fix x0 in it. For any x in F_y cap {0,1}^t, A(x-x0) = phi(x)-phi(x0) = 0 and x-x0 in D_t. The map x -> x-x0 is injective. So it maps F_y cap {0,1}^t into ker A cap D_t. Summing over fibres gives 2^t <= |im phi| |ker A cap D_t|. This refines COUNTING (which used {-1,0,1}^t, a superset of D_t). It is an upper bound on fibre size, not the lower bound G0006 asks for, so it does not close G0006 or G0004.

lemma: FIXED-MATRIX GATE LEMMA (linear SLP over F_p). Let M in F_p^{k x k} and let P be a straight-line program over F_p with inputs z_1..z_k, where each gate computes a linear form (a scalar multiple of an earlier form, or a sum of two earlier forms with coefficients in F_p), and the outputs are the k forms r_i = Row_i(M).z. Let N(M) be the number of distinct projective classes [r] over F_p of rows r_i with weight >= 2 (r is not a scalar multiple of a unit vector e_j). Then every such P has at least N(M) gates. PROOF: a row of weight >= 2 is not a scalar multiple of an input, so its output is some gate. Each gate computes one form, so distinct projective classes need distinct gates. Hence #gates >= N(M). SCOPE: fixed matrix M, linear programs over F_p, cost = number of gates (scalar multiples treated as free within the class). It is a bound per fixed matrix, not for a stream of updates.

As written the argument fails. Rechecking a candidate circuit against the past prefix needs that prefix, which is N = 2^m bits and cannot be stored in poly(s) space; keeping one consistent circuit does not decide which later candidates match the whole prefix. The conclusion survives via the repair lemma recorded next (residual-function automaton, unbounded update time, state count 2^{O(s log(m+s))}). Also the exact count r_t = |P_t| + [P_t != {0,1}^t] is not justified: distinct prefixes can have equal residuals, so only the upper bound r_t <= |P_t| + 1 is used. Lab: none (argument-level review). proved_step: REPAIR LEMMA for S0038 (CLAIMED). Fix m, s; N = 2^m; Circ_s = circuits on m inputs, binary gates, size <= s; |Circ_s| <= (16 (m+s)^2)^s (m+s) = 2^{O(s log(m+s))}. I_s = {Eval(C) : C in Circ_s} subset {0,1}^N; f(x) = lex-first C in Circ_s with Eval(C) = x, for x in I_s. For a prefix p of length t and q in {0,1}^(N-t) set g_p(q) = f(pq) if pq in I_s, else bottom. CLAIM: (a) for every block b of length l, g_{pb}(q) = g_p(bq) (directly from the definition), so the map (g_p, b) -> g_{pb} is a well-defined transition table depending only on m, s; (b) P_t = {p : g_p not identically bottom} = prefixes of Eval(C) for C in Circ_s, and assigning to each p in P_t its lex-first witness is injective into Circ_s, so the number of distinct g_p is at most |P_t| + 1 <= |Circ_s| + 1; (c) at t = N, g_x(empty) = f(x), so the final state contains the search output. Hence a one-pass automaton computes search-MCSP^A[s] (any A; no oracle needed for the bound) with ceil(log2(|Circ_s|+1)) = O(s log(m+s)) bits of state, unbounded update time (the transition table is a finite function of (m,s)). PROOF: (a) by the definition of g. (b) if g_p is not bottom, some Eval(C) has prefix p, so p is in P_t; distinct g_p values can be attached to a common witness only through the injection above, and bottom is one value, giving the count. (c) by definition. SCOPE: state-count bound for search-MCSP^A with unbounded update time. Does not give a poly-time update and does not close G0004 or G0009.

proved_step: LEMMA A (fast path) and LEMMA B (monotone witness). Setting: Circ_s = all straight-line circuits of size 1..s on m inputs, totally ordered by a fixed injective encoding ord. N = 2^m. Eval(C) in {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t, S(p) = {C : Eval(C) starts with p}, P_t = {p : S(p) nonempty}, and for p in P_t, w(p) = ord-least element of S(p). CLAIM A: if p in P_t, pb in P_{t+1}, and Eval(w(p))_{t+1} = b, then w(pb) = w(p). PROOF: w(p) has prefix pb, so w(p) is in S(pb). S(pb) is a subset of S(p), and w(p) is the least element of S(p), so it is also the least element of S(pb). QED. CLAIM B: if pb is in P_{t+1}, then w(p) <= w(pb). PROOF: S(pb) is a subset of S(p), so the minimum over S(p) is at most the minimum over S(pb). QED. COROLLARY: for a fixed Eval-string x, t -> w(x[:t]) is non-decreasing in ord. Scope: any total order on any circuit class; no complexity claim. CLASSIFICATION: Claim B and the corollary are bookkeeping, not progress. Claim A gives a per-step O(size(w(p))) fast path, but only when the bit matches.

evidence: Reviewed by hand, scope limited to the well-definedness of pi_t. Setting: a deterministic one-pass algorithm A reads x in {0,1}^N bit by bit, with state c_t in {0,1}^S, transitions c_{t+1} = g_t(c_t, x_{t+1}) (time-indexed), and output out(c_N) which is a function of the final state only. Correctness: out(c_N(x)) = f(x) for every input x in the promise set. Claim: if prefixes u, v of length t satisfy c_t(u) = c_t(v), then for every suffix w, c_N(uw) = c_N(vw) (induction on the suffix, since g_t depends only on the state and the next bit), so f(uw) = f(vw) for all w. Hence u and v have the same residual function and lie in the same Nerode class. Contrapositive: prefixes of different Nerode classes never share a code, so pi_t(code) := class of any prefix reaching the code is well defined. This argument does not use Satz B (S0010). Limits: (i) it needs the decision version, i.e. out is a function of f(x); for a search output (a circuit) the two-prefix argument only gives equal acceptable-answer sets, so the Nerode classes must then be defined by that; (ii) if correctness holds only on a promise set P, the residuals must be taken over suffixes that keep the input in P. proved_step: LINEAR-UPDATE DIMENSION LEMMA (restricted update class; closes nothing by itself, shrinks the linear case of G0004). Setting: F any field; N = 2^m; x in {0,1}^N; Im = Im_s = { truth tables of circuits of size <= s }; f = indicator of Im, valued in {0,1} inside F. A linear-update one-pass algorithm of dimension k over F: state s_0 in F^k fixed; s_t = A_{t,x_t} s_{t-1} for time-dependent matrices A_{t,b} in F^{k x k}; output c . s_N in F, required to equal f(x) for every x. (Affine updates are covered by adding one constant coordinate: dimension k+1.) Cut t: write x = p q with |p| = t, |q| = N - t. TRIANGULAR FOOLING SET at cut t: pairs (p_i, q_i), i = 1..r, with p_i q_i in Im for all i, and p_i q_j not in Im for all i > j (the cross entries with i < j are unconstrained). THEOREM: every such algorithm has k >= r. PROOF: for a prefix p let v_p = A_{t,p} s_0 in F^k, where A_{t,p} is the product of the prefix transitions (depends only on p). For a suffix q let w_q = B_{t,q}^T c in F^k, where B_{t,q} is the product of the suffix transitions (depends only on q). Then f(pq) = c . B_{t,q} A_{t,p} s_0 = <w_q, v_p>. So the r x r matrix M[i,j] = f(p_i q_j) equals V^T W with V = [v_{p_1} ... v_{p_r}] and W = [w_{q_1} ... w_{q_r}] in F^{k x r}, hence rank_F M <= k. By the fooling conditions M[i,i] = 1 and M[i,j] = 0 for i > j, so M is upper unitriangular with det 1 and rank_F M = r. Hence k >= r. QED. SCOPE: linear updates over a field, any time-dependent matrices, any N, any cut, any field; it says nothing about general or nonlinear updates and nothing about update time beyond the dimension. Note: the trivial bound rank_F M_t(f) <= |Im| does NOT give a lower bound; only a triangular fooling set (or any rank lower bound) does. CONSEQUENCE: the linear-update case of G0004 (poly(s) dimension cannot decide or search MCSP[s]) reduces to exhibiting, for some cut, a triangular fooling set of size superpolynomial in s inside Im_s. OPEN (not claimed): whether such a set exists. A max-degree greedy argument does not give it, because the prefix degree of Im can be comparable to |Im| (e.g. all circuits whose first cofactor is 0). GAP: G0004 (restricted class only; general update time open); no claim about P vs NP.

proved_step: CAP LEMMA (cut-rank cap). Let S be any set of N-bit truth tables, N=2^m. (a) For every 1<=t<N and every field F, rank_F M_t(S) <= |S|, where M_t[p][q]=1[(q<<t)|p in S]. Proof: each f in S sets exactly one entry of M_t, so M_t has at most |S| nonzero entries, hence at most |S| nonzero rows, and rank <= number of nonzero rows. (b) For S=Im_s, |Im_s| <= (16(m+s)^2)^s, since a size-<=s circuit is a sequence of at most s gates, each choosing an op (16) and two earlier nodes (at most (m+i)^2 choices for gate i). (c) For the prefix Myhill-Nerode classes of S at level t: the residual of prefix p is zero unless p is a prefix of some element of S, and distinct nonzero residuals need distinct prefixes, so the number of classes is at most |S|+1. Hence the minimal exact prefix automaton of Im_s has at most |Im_s|+1 states per level, i.e. O(s log(m+s)) bits, which is inside the budget O(log N + s log(n+s)). Consequence: a cut-rank lower bound on the STATE count of this automaton cannot exceed O(s log(m+s)) bits. The S0098 route (k >= rank_F) therefore bounds only LINEAR-dimension models; it cannot establish a streaming lower bound beyond the budget, consistent with the protocol's statement that only an update-time lower bound can.

proved_step: REPAIR LEMMA (residual-function automaton for EXT prefix language). Let N = 2^m, s <= poly(m). For a prefix p of length t <= N, define the residual language R_p = { q in {0,1}^{N-t} : p q in Im_s } where Im_s is the set of truth tables of fan-in-2 circuits of size <= s over m inputs. (a) The number of distinct residual languages is at most |Im_s| + 1 <= (16(m+s)^2)^s + 1. Proof: distinct nonempty residuals correspond to distinct nonempty subsets of Im_s sharing the same prefix p, so there are at most |Im_s| of them; the empty residual (p not a prefix of any element of Im_s) adds at most one. (b) The minimal exact prefix automaton of the language Im_s therefore has at most |Im_s| + 1 states per level t, and total states at most (N+1)(|Im_s|+1). State bits per level: log2(|Im_s|+1) <= s log2(16(m+s)^2) + 1 = O(s log(m+s)). (c) The state transition function (update) given a new bit b: from state representing residual R, go to the state representing R.b = { q' : b q' in R }. Computing this update may require time exponential in s (unbounded update time), because testing whether a string q' is in R.b means checking whether p b q' in Im_s, i.e., whether a given truth table prefix extends to a circuit of size <= s. No poly(s) time update is claimed. (d) This automaton is exactly the Myhill-Nerode DFA of the language Im_s, and its state count at level t equals the number of Myhill-Nerode equivalence classes of prefixes of length t. The earlier claim r_t = |P_t| + [P_t != {0,1}^t] is corrected to r_t <= |P_t| + 1 where P_t is the set of length-t prefixes of Im_s, and the inequality can be strict because distinct prefixes may yield the same residual. (e) Consequence: any streaming algorithm that decides membership in Im_s must use at least log2(|Im_s|+1) bits of state, but this lower bound is only O(s log(m+s)) bits, which is inside the O(log N + s log(n+s)) budget of the MMW19 Thm 1.2 algorithm. Hence a state-count lower bound alone cannot separate the EXT automaton from the budget. To obtain a separation, an UPDATE-TIME lower bound is needed, consistent with G0004.

proved_step: REPAIR of S0038 (state count only, no update-time claim). Setting: Im_s = set of truth tables of all nodes (inputs and gates) of circuits of size <= s over m inputs, N = 2^m. For t in 0..N, M_t = 2^t - 1, P_t = {f & M_t : f in Im_s}, and for p in {0,1}^t the residual R_p = {f >> t : f in Im_s, f & M_t = p}. CLAIM A: the number D_t of distinct residual sets satisfies D_t <= |P_t| + 1 <= |Im_s| + 1. PROOF: R_p is empty when p is not in P_t, so each nonempty residual set is R_p for some p in P_t, and the empty set adds at most one class. CLAIM B: |Im_s| <= 3(4(m+s)^2)^s. PROOF: at step k (0 <= k < s) a circuit has L_k <= m+s nodes, and the number of candidate new gates is at most L_k (negations) + 3 L_k^2 (ordered and, or, xor) <= a := 4(m+s)^2. Gate-creating choice sequences of length <= s number at most sum_{k=1}^{s} a^k <= 2a^s (a >= 2). Adding the m inputs gives |Im_s| <= m + 2a^s <= 3a^s. COROLLARY: D_t <= 3(4(m+s)^2)^s + 1, so log D_t = O(s log(m+s)) bits. SCOPE: state count of the prefix automaton of EXT_{m,s}; no update-time bound, so G0003 and G0004 remain open. proved_step: Lemma L1 (bit-level residual transition). Proof: the level-(t+1) residual of an extended prefix is obtained by restricting the level-t residual to the assignments whose next bit equals b and then dropping that bit (shift by one). Restriction to bit value b selects exactly g in R_p with g&1 = b, and the shift g>>1 re-indexes the remaining bits. This is a direct unfolding of the residual definition, not a counting argument. Computational check: cm-2b9d70b2910543ec, exhaustive for (m,s) in {(2,1),(2,2),(3,1),(3,2)} and n_fails = 0 on all cases, plus m=4, s=1 with 131070 checks and n_fails = 0.

lemma: REPAIR OF S0038 (state count). Setting: n>=1, s>=1, N=2^n, Im = {tt(C) : C a circuit on n inputs of size <= s} subset {0,1}^N, M = |Im|. For 0<=t<=N and a prefix p in {0,1}^t define the residual R_p = {q in {0,1}^(N-t) : pq in Im}. CLAIM: the number of distinct residuals {R_p : p in {0,1}^t} is at most M+1, and log(M+1) = O(s log(n+s)). PROOF: Let T_t = {p in {0,1}^t : R_p nonempty} = set of length-t prefixes of elements of Im; |T_t| <= M. For p not in T_t, R_p is the empty set, giving one residual. The map p -> R_p restricted to T_t has image of size <= |T_t| <= M. Hence the total is <= M+1. For the bound on M: a circuit of size <= s on n inputs is determined by at most s gates, each given by a gate type and two inputs from at most n+s earlier nodes plus an output choice, so the number of such circuits is at most (c(n+s)^2)^(s+1) for a constant c, and M is at most this. So log M = O(s log(n+s)).

For a prefix p of length t and residual R_p = {q in {0,1}^(N-t) : pq in Im}, the following hold exactly. (i) For b in {0,1}: R_{pb} = {q' in {0,1}^(N-t-1) : bq' in R_p}, i.e. R_{pb} is the b-cofactor of R_p at its first coordinate. Proof: pbq' in Im iff bq' in R_p, by definition of R_p. (ii) R_{pb} is empty iff EXT_{n,s}(pb)=1 is false, where EXT_{n,s}(x)=1 iff some circuit of size <= s has truth table with prefix x. Proof: by definition. (iii) Hence the Myhill-Nerode classes of the prefix language of Im (read most-significant bit first) form a deterministic automaton whose state count is at most M+1 (the bound of G0062), and whose transition on bit b is the cofactor map on classes. Proof: (i) shows the transition is determined by R_p, and the state count is the G0062 bound.

proved_step: LEMMA (exponential-time update, not poly(s)). Setting: n>=1, s>=1, N=2^n, Im = {tt(C): C circuit on n inputs, size <= s}. For any prefix p of length t, EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff some C in Im has prefix p. PROOF: Every circuit of size <= s over binary fan-in gates is specified by at most s gates; gate k has an op from a set of 16 binary Boolean functions and two inputs among the n+k-1 earlier nodes, plus a choice of output node. So the number of circuits is at most (16 (n+s)^2)^(s+1). Each truth table has N bits and is computed in poly(N) * s time by evaluating gates on N-bit words. Enumerating all circuits and checking prefix p therefore decides EXT_{n,s}(p) in time (16 (n+s)^2)^(s+1) * poly(N). The update for bit b on state p is one such query, so the update time is 2^{O(s log(n+s))} * poly(2^n). SCOPE: a general upper bound, exponential in s. It does NOT bound update time by poly(s), so it does not close G0003 (which needs poly(s) update) and does not touch G0004 (a lower bound).

proved_step: LEMMA R (rank form of the linear-update bound; tightens S0098 from a triangular fooling set to the full cut rank). Setting: F a field, N = 2^m, Im = Im_s as in S0098, f = indicator of Im valued in F. A linear-update one-pass algorithm of dimension k over F computes f on {0,1}^N. Fix a cut t and let M_t be the 2^t x 2^(N-t) matrix M_t[p,q] = f(pq) over F. CLAIM: k >= rank_F(M_t) for every t. PROOF: the transitions A_{i,b} are fixed per position i, so for a prefix p of length t the state after reading p is v_p = A_{t,p} s_0 in F^k, where A_{t,p} is the ordered product of the prefix transitions. For a suffix q of length N-t, the remaining transitions give s_N = B_q v_p with B_q in F^{k x k} depending only on q. The output is c . s_N, so f(pq) = u_q . v_p with u_q = c B_q in F^(1 x k). Hence M_t = U V where U has rows u_q (2^(N-t) x k) and V has columns v_p (k x 2^t), so rank_F M_t <= k. COROLLARY: k >= max_t rank_F M_t, which is at least the size of any triangular fooling set (the upper-triangular principal submatrix with unit diagonal has det 1). SCOPE: exact for linear-update algorithms over the field F; the bound is field-dependent in general: rank_Q and rank_{F_p} of an integer matrix can differ (rank_{F_p} <= rank_Q), so the bound for an F_p-algorithm must use rank over F_p. Does not give a poly-time or update-time bound, does not close G0004. Upper limit: rank_F M_t <= min(2^t, 2^(N-t), |Im_s|) with |Im_s| = 2^(O(s log(m+s))), so the rank bound cannot exceed the circuit-count bound of S0091 in magnitude.

proved_step: LEMMA L1 (fixed-s streaming for membership in Im_s; bookkeeping, not progress). Setting: m, s >= 1; Circ_s = straight-line programs of length k, 1 <= k <= s, where step j (j = 1..k) applies one of the 4 ops {AND, OR, XOR, a&~b} to a pair a < b of the m+j-1 earlier nodes. Im_s = truth tables of Circ_s. (i) COUNT: a program of length k is determined by its sequence of choices (op_j, a_j, b_j), and there are at most 4*C(m+j-1,2) <= 2(m+s)^2 choices at step j, so the number of programs of length k is at most (2(m+s)^2)^k, and |Circ_s| <= sum_{k=1..s} (2(m+s)^2)^k <= 2(2(m+s)^2)^s, since the ratio r = 2(m+s)^2 >= 2 makes the geometric sum at most 2 r^s. (ii) ALGORITHM: read x_1..x_N in order and keep the alive set A_t = {C in Circ_s : C(y) = x_y for all y <= t}, stored as a bit vector of length |Circ_s|. Start with A_0 = Circ_s. At step t, for each alive C, compute C(y_t) for the input y_t with binary expansion t in O(s+m) time, and drop C if it differs from x_t. Then A_N = {C : Eval(C) = x}, and the output is 1 iff A_N is nonempty. (iii) CORRECTNESS: by induction on t, A_t is exactly the consistent set, so the output decides x in Im_s exactly. (iv) COST: state |Circ_s| bits, per-bit time O(|Circ_s|(s+m)), so for fixed s both are poly(m) with degree O(s). For s = m^c the bound is 2^{Theta(s log m)}, superpolynomial. PROOF COMPLETE for (i)-(iv). SCOPE: membership in Im_s for fixed s only. Does NOT bound the update cost for s = poly(m), and does NOT close G0004 or G0071-G0074. Its state bound is the trivial one; the O(s log(m+s)) bit bound would need S0091, which is still unreviewed. proved_step: LEMMA (state count of the EXT prefix automaton, restricted class B, |B|=b). Let B be a finite binary basis (here AND, OR, XOR, so b=3; no negation or constants), let N=2^m, let C_{m,s} be the circuits of size <= s over inputs x_1..x_m with fan-in-2 gates from B, and let Im_{m,s} subset {0,1}^N be their truth tables. Then (a) |Im_{m,s}| <= prod_{k=0}^{s-1} b(m+k)(m+k+1)/2 <= (b(m+s)^2)^s. (b) For every t in 0..N and every prefix p in {0,1}^t, let R_t(p) = {w in {0,1}^{N-t} : pw in Im}. The number of distinct nonempty R_t(p) is at most |Im_{m,s}|. Hence the minimal (Myhill-Nerode) automaton reading the truth table has at most |Im_{m,s}| states at each level, i.e. log(#states) = O(s log(m+s)) bits, plus log N bits for the position counter. PROOF (a): a circuit of size s is determined by the sequence of gates; gate k picks an unordered pair {i<=j} from the m+k available nodes and one of b operations, giving at most b(m+k)(m+k+1)/2 choices; the map from sequences to truth tables is onto Im, so |Im| is at most the product. PROOF (b): restriction to the first t bits maps Im onto the set of realised prefixes, so #realised prefixes <= |Im|; R_t(p) depends only on p, so the number of distinct residuals is at most the number of realised prefixes. Both steps are elementary counting.

proved_step: PROOF. (1) rank_F M <= |S|: rank is at most the number of nonzero rows; each nonzero row holds at least one 1; the map x -> (x>>(N-t), x mod 2^(N-t)) is injective and each x in S sets exactly one entry, so the number of 1-entries is |S|. Hence rank_F M_t(S) <= |S| for every field F. (2) |Im_s| bound: every function in Im_s is the value of some gate of a program with j <= s gates (or a base node). A program of j gates is a sequence where gate k (1<=k<=j) is op_c(a,b) with c in [16] and a,b among the m+2+(k-1) = m+1+k earlier nodes. So the number of programs with j gates is at most prod_{k=1}^{j} 16(m+1+k)^2 <= (16(m+s+1)^2)^j, because m+1+k <= m+s+1 for k <= s. The base nodes contribute at most m+2 <= 16(m+s+1)^2 values. Summing over j=0..s: |Im_s| <= sum_{j=0}^{s} (16(m+s+1)^2)^j <= (s+1)(16(m+s+1)^2)^s. Combining (1) and (2) gives the lemma. proved_step: LEMMA (F_2 affine images: streaming membership). Let r, L >= 1, M_1..M_L in F_2^r (row vectors), c in F_2^L, and phi(z)_t = <M_t, z> + c_t for z in F_2^r. Let Im = phi(F_2^r). For a prefix p of length t, p is a prefix of some element of Im iff the linear system {<M_s, z> = p_s + c_s : s <= t} is consistent over F_2. Maintain the reduced row-echelon basis of the augmented system (rows (M_s | p_s + c_s)), with at most r pivots. Appending bit b to p is one insertion: reduce the new augmented row by the existing pivot rows (at most r XORs of (r+1)-bit words), declare p dead iff the reduced row is 0 with rhs 1, otherwise add it as a new pivot and clear its pivot column from the other rows. Correctness: the system is consistent iff no F_2-combination of its rows gives 0 = 1; the reduced echelon basis spans exactly the row space of the augmented system, so it detects inconsistency. Consequences: (i) x in {0,1}^L lies in Im iff the full system with rhs x_s + c_s is consistent, decidable in one pass with state O(r^2) bits and update time O(r^2) word operations per bit, with no exponential branching needed; (ii) the trie of Im restricted to affine images is poly-state per prefix. SCOPE: F_2 affine images only, z over all of F_2^r (no circuit, no size bound s). It does NOT address G0004, which concerns Im(Eval) of circuits of size <= s, where the extension question is an existential over Circ_s. This is standard Gaussian elimination, recorded as a restricted-class special case; it is bookkeeping and does not count as progress toward P vs NP. Setting: N=2^m, x in {0,1}^N, Im_1 = truth tables of circuits of size <= 1 on m inputs over binary gates {AND, OR, XOR, a&~b}, plus constants and literals. PROOF: induction on t, alive_t = {c : c agrees with x on positions < t}; at t=N the agreement is equality. Per-bit update costs O(|alive_t|) <= O(m^2) = O(log^2 N) comparisons; state is one bit per candidate, O(m^2) bits. SCOPE: size <= 1 only. Its per-bit cost is poly(log N) only because |Im_1| is polynomial; for general s, |Circ_s| = 2^{Theta(s log(m+s))}, so this filter is superpolynomial in m when s = poly(m). proved_step: REPAIR of S0057 (state-count form). Setting: p=3, t,k>=1, A in F_3^{k x t}, c in F_3^k, phi(x)=Ax+c, B={0,1}^t, K(A):=|ker A ∩ {-1,0,1}^t|. CLAIM: (i) 2^t <= |phi(B)| * K(A); (ii) if K(A)=1 then phi is injective on B. PROOF of (i): for v in phi(B) let F_v = B ∩ phi^{-1}(v). Fix x0 in F_v. For x in F_v, A(x-x0)=phi(x)-phi(x0)=0 and every coordinate of x-x0 lies in {-1,0,1}, so x -> x-x0 maps F_v injectively into ker A ∩ {-1,0,1}^t, giving |F_v| <= K(A). The fibres F_v partition B, so 2^t = sum_v |F_v| <= |phi(B)| K(A). PROOF of (ii): if phi(x)=phi(y) with x,y in B, then x-y in ker A with coordinates in {-1,0,1}, so x-y in ker A ∩ {-1,0,1}^t = {0} (K(A)=1 and 0 is always in the set), hence x=y. QED. SCOPE: F_3 only, one affine map, state-count bookkeeping. It gives no fibre lower bound, no update-time bound, and does not close G0004 or G0009. proved_step: LEMMA K-BOUND (kind LEMMA). Let F = F_p, p prime, A a k x t matrix over F, K(A) = |ker A cap {-1,0,1}^t| with -1 read in F, r = rank A. Then K(A) <= 3^(t-r). PROOF: ker A is a subspace of dimension d = t - r. Choose a set S of d coordinates such that the projection pi_S: ker A -> F^S is injective (exists: a basis of ker A, as a d x t matrix, has d linearly independent columns S, and then pi_S is an isomorphism onto F^d). For y in ker A cap {-1,0,1}^t, y is determined by pi_S(y), and pi_S(y) lies in {-1,0,1}^S, which has 3^d elements. Hence K(A) <= 3^d. Consequence: |phi(B)| >= 2^t / K(A) >= (2/3)^t * 3^r ... more precisely |phi(B)| >= 2^t / 3^(t-r). Tightness: equality K(A)=3^(t-r) is attained on the tested instances (max ratio 1.0, cm-4a7a793493bf40c0). SCOPE: a state-count bound for a linear map on the Boolean cube; no update-time bound; does not close G0004 or G0009. Refutes nothing new. Hypothesis H_gap (K(A) <= 3^(t-r) fails for p >= 5) is refuted by the same argument, not only by the sample.

proved_step: PROCEDURE UPD (exact bit-streaming update of the EXT prefix automaton, claimed by R1460). Setting: N = 2^m, Circ_s = all straight-line circuits of size 1..s on m inputs (gate lists, output = last gate), totally ordered by list index ord. Truth tables Eval(C) in {0,1}^N. The state after reading prefix p of length t is w(p) = ord-least C with Eval(C) starting with p, if one exists. STATE: the single circuit w (encoding O(s log(m+s)) bits) plus the counter t (log N bits). CLAIM: UPD(w, b) := ord-least C in Circ_s with Eval(C)[0..t] = Eval(w)[0..t-1] . b computes w(pb) exactly. PROOF: (i) Eval(w)[0..t-1] = p, since w(p) starts with p by definition, so p is recoverable from the state. (ii) {C : Eval(C) starts with pb} = {C : Eval(C) starts with p and Eval(C)_t = b} is exactly the set the scan tests, so the scan returns min S(pb) = w(pb). (iii) If no C matches, S(pb) is empty and the stream is dead. RUNNING TIME: scanning costs at most |Circ_s| candidates; each prefix test evaluates a candidate on assignments 0..t, which is O((t+1) s) word operations. With |Circ_s| <= 2(16(m+s)^2)^s (each gate: 16 ops and at most (m+s)^2 operand pairs), one bit costs O((16(m+s)^2)^s (t+1) s) operations and N bits cost O((16(m+s)^2)^s N^2 s). SCOPE: exact for every m, s; the time is polynomial in N for fixed s but exponential in s, so it does NOT give poly(s) per-bit update and does NOT close G0004 or G0003. It shows that the update function is computable from the O(s log(m+s))-bit state plus t, with an explicit bound. OPEN: whether the scan over Circ_s can be replaced by a search of size poly(s) (this is the content of G0004).

lemma: Lemma C (mismatch-only change). Let Circ_s be the size<=s straight-line circuits on m inputs with a fixed total order ord, S(p) = {C : Eval(C) starts with p}, and w(p) = ord-least element of S(p). If p in P_t, pb in P_{t+1}, and Eval(w(p))_{t+1} = b, then w(pb) = w(p). Equivalently, w(pb) != w(p) only if Eval(w(p))_{t+1} != b. Proof: w(p) has prefix pb, so w(p) is in S(pb) subset of S(p); being the least element of the larger set S(p), it is the least of S(pb). QED.

Index truth tables of m-bit inputs by x in {0,1}^m as an integer in 0..N-1, N=2^m, and let bit t be the value at index t. lemma: POINTER-SCAN LEMMA (update cost of the EXT prefix automaton, one fixed target string). Setting: Circ_s = all straight-line circuits of size 1..s on m inputs, listed in a fixed order ord; Eval(C) is the N-bit truth table, N=2^m; for a target x in {0,1}^N and t in 1..N, w_t(x) = least index C with Eval(C) starting with x[:t] (undefined if none). Claim: w_t(x) is non-decreasing in t, and a single forward pointer i, started at 0 and advanced while Eval(circ_i) does not start with x[:t], finds w_t(x) for every t with total advances <= |Circ_s|. Proof: the set of circuits matching prefix t is contained in the set matching prefix t-1, so every circuit with index < w_{t-1}(x) fails prefix t-1 and hence prefix t; the scan from w_{t-1} therefore reaches the least match at level t. The pointer never moves backwards, so the total number of advances is at most |Circ_s|. SCOPE: time |Circ_s| * poly(N) for one whole string.

lemma: LEMMA-AMORT (general, exact): Fix any sorted list T_0 < ... < T_{K-1} of N-bit strings and any x in {0,1}^N. For t in [0,N) let S_t = {i : T_i[0..t] = x[0..t]}. Then S_{t+1} is a subset of S_t, so w_t = min S_t is non-decreasing in t. The forward scan (keep pointer w; at step t, test T_w against prefix t and advance w while it mismatches) answers EXT for every prefix t (is S_t nonempty) with at most K + N prefix tests in total. Proof: indices below w are outside S_{t-1}, hence outside S_t, so skipping them is safe, and the first match is min S_t. w only increases and stops at K, so there are at most K advances; each step t ends with at most one failing test, giving at most N of those. Total <= K + N.

(iii) Computing the k-th circuit's table needs the listing, which costs 2^{O(s log(m+s))} time, not a per-bit step.

CLAIM 1 (correctness): SCAN(x) returns the ord-least C with prefix x, i.e. w(x) as defined in S0095, or NONE iff x is not live. CLAIM 2 (space): the enumerator is a mixed-radix counter over gate sequences of length at most s, using O(s log(m+s)) bits of workspace plus O(log N) for the index t. CLAIM 3 (time): |Circ_s| <= sum_{k<=s} (16 (m+s)^2)^k <= 2 (16 (m+s)^2)^s, and each Eval costs O(s N / w) word operations. proved_step: CONSTANT-s STREAMING UPDATE LEMMA (scope: fixed m >= 1, fixed s >= 1). Let Circ_s(m) be the straight-line circuits with at most s fan-in-2 gates over {AND, OR, XOR, ANDNOT} on inputs x_0..x_{m-1}; N = 2^m; Eval(C) in {0,1}^N. Claims: (i) L_0() = Circ_s(m); (ii) L_{t+1}(pb) = {C in L_t(p) : Eval(C)_t = b}; (iii) EXT(p) = 1 iff L_t(p) is nonempty; (iv) |Circ_s(m)| <= (s+1)(4(m+s)^2)^s. PROOF: (i) and (iii) are definitions. (ii): C is in L_{t+1}(pb) iff Eval(C)_a = p_a for a < t and Eval(C)_t = b, which is C in L_t(p) with Eval(C)_t = b. (iv): a circuit with k gates has at most prod_{i<k} 4*C(m+i,2) <= (4(m+s)^2)^k choices, since gate i picks one of 4 ops and an unordered pair among m+i <= m+s nodes; summing over k = 0..s gives (s+1)(4(m+s)^2)^s. COST: storing L_t as a membership bitmap over Circ_s(m) takes |Circ_s(m)| bits. One update evaluates each circuit at the single assignment bin(t), which takes O(s) bit operations per circuit, so the worst-case per-bit time is O(s (s+1) (4(m+s)^2)^s), which is poly(m) = poly(log N) when s = O(1). lemma: LEMMA (prefix-read bound, kind LEMMA, unconditional). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates over inputs x=(y,z), y in {0,1}^t the prefix, z the rest. Let R be the set of prefix indices i such that y_i feeds a gate directly, so |R| <= 2s. Then for every fixed prefix assignment rho, the residual C|_rho(z) depends only on rho restricted to R. Hence D_t(C) := #{C|_rho : rho in {0,1}^t} <= min(2^t, 2^{2s}). PROOF: induct on gates in topological order. A gate whose two input wires are both not prefix wires computes a function of z-wires and earlier gates only, so its value is independent of rho. A gate with a prefix input wire y_i has i in R, so its value depends on rho only through rho_i. Downstream gates take values that depend on rho only through rho|_R, so the output does too. The bound D_t <= 2^{|R|} follows because the residual is a function of rho|_R. QED.
gap: G0118 is NOT closed. This lemma gives the exponential bound 2^{2s} only. The target is D_t <= |Im_s|+1 or D_t <= poly(s) uniformly in m and t. The remaining obstacle: many distinct rho|_R patterns can still give the same residual function, and no argument in this session shows they collapse to poly(s) classes. Next step: prove a collapse lemma. Candidate: two patterns rho, rho' on R give the same residual iff they agree on the set of gates whose values are 'live' for the residual, which should give a count of at most (number of live gate-value vectors) <= poly(s).

lemma: CORRECTED LEMMA (repair of S0219, kind LEMMA, unconditional). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates over inputs x=(y,z), y in {0,1}^t the prefix. Let R = set of prefix indices i such that y_i is an input of some gate, or is the output wire. Then |R| <= 2s+1 (each gate has 2 input wires, plus 1 for the output). For every prefix rho, C|_rho(z) depends only on rho|_R. Hence D_t(C) <= min(2^t, 2^{2s+1}). PROOF: induction over gates in topological order, as in S0219. A gate with no prefix input wire is independent of rho. A gate with prefix input wire y_i has i in R, so its value depends only on rho_i. Downstream values depend only on rho|_R. The output wire is either a gate value (handled above) or a prefix wire y_i with i in R, which depends only on rho_i. QED. Edge case: s=0, output y_1 gives R={1}, D=2 <= 2^{1} = 2^{2s+1}, consistent. S0219 as stated (bound 2^{2s}) FAILS at s=0 because it omits the output-wire case; the corrected bound 2^{2s+1} replaces it.

refuted_approach: G0119 collapse target: per-circuit residual count D_t(C) <= poly(s) is REFUTED. Under prefix rho the residual is OR_{i: rho_i=1} z_i. PROOF of exact count: for distinct supports S != S' pick i in the symmetric difference; z = e_i gives residuals 1 and 0, so they differ. Hence D_t(C_k) = 2^k = 2^{(s+1)/2} exactly. Standard circuit simulation of a space-S, time-U computation (per step): each step's update reads 1 input bit, updates S-bit state in U time steps. Unroll into U layers of configurations (each S bits). Each time step's transition is local (each output bit depends on O(1) input bits), implemented by O(1) fan-in-2 gates per bit. Total gates per step = U layers * S bits * O(1) gates = O(U*S). This is a standard Cook-style simulation bound, correct.

gap: G0004 reformulated. For N=2^n and a full-length prefix p (t=N), EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff tt(p) in Im_s, i.e. full-length prefix extension is MCSP membership at threshold s. Hence any exact uniform update U(state,b) of time poly(s,n) per bit, applied over the N bits, decides MCSP[s] in N*poly(s,n) time; for s=m^c this is poly(N). A worst-case poly(s,m) per-bit bound for growing s therefore implies a polynomial-time algorithm for MCSP at polynomial threshold, which is open. G0004 is thus NOT a streaming-only shortcut: it is at least as hard as an algorithmic result on the target's own problem. Hypotheses to check: uniformity of U, and exactness of the state (the state determines R_p up to equivalence).

Gate k (k=1..s) takes an ordered pair of nodes among the n+k-1 <= n+s-1 nodes already present (at most (n+s)^2 choices) and one of 16 binary Boolean operations, giving at most 16(n+s)^2 choices per gate. evidence: Counting lemma (corrected Lemma C). Let n,s >= 1 and Im = {tt(C) : C an n-input circuit of size <= s} over binary fan-in gates with 16 ops. Let B = 16(n+s)^2. A circuit of size k has, for gate j, at most 16(n+j-1)^2 <= B choices (op and ordered input pair among n+j-1 earlier nodes), and at most n+s output choices. So the number of (circuit, output) pairs of size exactly k is at most (n+s) B^k. Summing over k = 0..s and using B >= 16 (geometric series, sum_{k<=s} B^k <= 2 B^s) gives |Im| <= 2(n+s) B^s = 2(n+s)(16(n+s)^2)^s. Hence log2|Im| <= 1 + log2(n+s) + s(4 + 2 log2(n+s)) = O(s log(n+s)). Scope: bounds the number of distinct residual states only. Does not bound update time, so G0003 (poly(s) update) stays open. proved_step: LEMMA (complement closure). For n>=1, s>=1, Im_{n,s} = {tt(C) : C a circuit on n inputs of size <= s} is closed under bitwise complement. Proof: let C have size k <= s. If k >= 1, replace the op of the output gate by its complement (the map f -> NOT f on the 16 binary ops is an involution). The new circuit has size k and computes the complement of tt(C). If k = 0, the output is a leaf x_i or a constant. The complement of a constant is a constant (already a size-0 circuit), and NOT x_i = NAND(x_i, x_i) is one gate, allowed since s >= 1. Hence the complement lies in Im_{n,s}. Consequence: EXT_{n,s}(p) = EXT_{n,s}(p-bar) for every prefix p, where p-bar is the bitwise complement. SCOPE: a closure property of the set only. It bounds neither update time nor state count. It does not close G0003 (poly(s) update) or G0004 (update-time lower bound). Trivial bookkeeping lemma; not counted as progress.

lemma: LEMMA (repaired state count). n,s>=1, N=2^n, Im subset {0,1}^N, M=|Im|. For t in 0..N and prefix p of length t let R_p = {q in {0,1}^(N-t): pq in Im}. Then the family {R_p : |p|=t} has at most M+1 distinct members, and the family over all t has at most (N+1)(M+1) members. PROOF: R_p is nonempty iff p is a length-t prefix of some word of Im; the set P_t of such realized prefixes has |P_t| <= M (each word has one t-prefix). Distinct nonempty residuals at level t are indexed by P_t, so at most M of them; add the empty residual: M+1 per level, and N+1 levels. Hence the Myhill-Nerode states of the prefix language have at most (N+1)(M+1) classes, and with |Im| <= 2(n+s)(16(n+s)^2)^s (S0091 bound) this is O(log N + s log(n+s)) bits. proved_step: Field dependence of cut ranks is exactly the prime divisors of the Smith invariant factors. For A in {0,1}^{RxC} with r = rank_Q(A): (1) rank_{F_p}(A) = #{i<=r : p does not divide d_i}; (2) Delta_r(A) = d_1...d_r <= r^{r/2} (Hadamard); (3) rank_{F_p}(A) = rank_Q(A) for every prime p > r^{r/2}. Proof: Smith normal form and reduction mod p; Delta_r divides each nonzero r-minor; Hadamard row-norm bound.

The counting argument is sound: (1) Number of circuits of size ≤ s over n inputs with 16 binary Boolean operations: each of the s gates chooses an operation (16 choices) and two inputs from n+k-1 ≤ n+s-1 earlier nodes, giving ≤ 16(n+s)^2 choices per gate. The output chooses from n+s nodes. Total ≤ (16(n+s)^2)^s * (n+s) ≤ (16(n+s)^2)^(s+1) for n,s ≥ 1. (2) Each circuit evaluates on all 2^n inputs in O(2^n * s) bit operations by word-level evaluation. (3) Checking a prefix p of length t requires evaluating all circuits and comparing prefixes. Total decision time ≤ (16(n+s)^2)^(s+1) * poly(2^n). This is a valid general upper bound, exponential in s. The scope correctly notes it does not achieve poly(s) update time required by G0003. No counterexample exists for this counting bound; it is a standard circuit enumeration argument.

The aligned-prefix restriction lemma is correct. For the subset direction: given an n-input circuit C of size ≤ s, substituting 0 for variables x_{k+1..n} yields a k-input circuit (some gates may become constant or degenerate but gate count doesn't increase). For the superset direction: any k-input circuit of size ≤ s trivially works as an n-input circuit ignoring extra inputs. The sets are exactly equal. The consequence about EXT query at aligned length 2^k reducing to MCSP-membership on 2^k-bit tables is valid. Scope correctly notes this doesn't close G0003 (needs poly(s) update). No counterexample.

The amortized witness automaton lemma is correct as an amortized bound. w_t is non-decreasing in t because as the prefix grows, the set of circuits matching it shrinks, so the ord-least circuit can only stay the same or increase. Total circuit checks ≤ |Circ_s| + N because each circuit is checked at most once (when w_t advances to it) plus N prefix checks. Each check costs O(N poly(m+s)). This gives total time for one fixed input, not a per-update worst-case bound. Correctly scoped - does not close G0003 or G0004. No counterexample.

The rank form lemma is correct for linear-update algorithms over field F. The state after prefix p is v_p = A_{t,p} s_0 ∈ F^k. The output is c·B_q v_p = u_q·v_p with u_q = c B_q. So M_t[p,q] = f(pq) = u_q·v_p, hence M_t = U V where U (2^{N-t} × k) has rows u_q and V (k × 2^t) has columns v_p. Therefore rank_F(M_t) ≤ k. This is a standard linear-algebraic lower bound for linear streaming algorithms. The corollary about triangular fooling sets follows because a triangular submatrix with unit diagonal has full rank. The note about field-dependent rank (rank_{F_p} ≤ rank_Q for integer matrices) is important and correct. Scope correctly states this doesn't give a poly(s) update bound. No counterexample.

Reviewed the counting argument and algorithm of Lemma L1 (S0144). COUNT: At step j (1..k<=s), there are 4 operations {AND,OR,XOR,a&~b} applied to an unordered pair from m+j-1 earlier nodes. Number of choices <= 4*C(m+j-1,2) <= 2(m+s)^2. Programs of length k: <= (2(m+s)^2)^k. Sum_{k=1..s} <= 2(2(m+s)^2)^s (geometric series, ratio >=2). This upper bound is correct (loose by at most factor 2 for a&~b since order matters but bound uses unordered pairs). ALGORITHM: Maintain bit vector A_t of length |Circ_s|, initially all 1. At step t, for each circuit C in Circ_s, compute C(y_t) where y_t is the t-th input (binary expansion of t) in O(s+m) time, zero the bit if C(y_t) != x_t. After N=2^m steps, A_N nonempty iff x in Im_s. CORRECTNESS: By induction on t, A_t = {C: C agrees with x on first t inputs}. COST: State = |Circ_s| bits = O((m+s)^{2s}) bits. Per-bit update time = O(|Circ_s|*(s+m)). For FIXED s, both are poly(m) with degree O(s). For s = m^c, state = 2^{Theta(s log m)} superpolynomial. The lemma explicitly states scope: fixed s only, does NOT bound update cost for s=poly(m), does NOT close G0004/G0071-G0074. All claims in the stated scope are correct. No counterexample found.

lemma: Let N=2^m, Im_s = {truth tables of circuits of size <= s on m inputs}, and for a prefix p of length t let R_p = {q in {0,1}^(N-t) : pq in Im_s}. (a) If R_p != R_p' then no streaming algorithm that reads the prefix can end in the same memory state on p and p'. (b) Hence any deterministic streaming decider for prefix-extendability of Im_s needs at least ceil(log2 #{R_p : p a prefix}) bits of memory at some time. Proof of (a): pick q in R_p symmetric-difference R_p'; the continuations pq and p'q differ in acceptance, so the states after p and p' must differ. (b) follows from (a) by pigeonhole. SCOPE: streaming memory only, no update-time bound, no claim about circuits beyond Im_s. Parts (2) and (3) of the task (transition cost as gates on H_C, and bridging to arbitrary MCSP circuits) are NOT addressed here.

lemma: LEMMA (space upper bound, EXT). Let N=2^m, Im_s = truth tables of circuits with <= s binary gates (16 ops) on m inputs, P_t = length-t prefixes of Im_s, R_p = {q : pq in Im_s}. Then (1) |P_t| <= |Im_s| for all t; (2) #{R_p : p in {0,1}^t} <= |Im_s|+1; (3) |Im_s| <= (16(m+s)^2)^s, so ceil(log2(|Im_s|+1)) <= s(4+2log2(m+s))+1 = O(s log(m+s)). Proof: (1) truncation maps Im_s onto P_t. (2) R_p is empty iff p not in P_t (one class); otherwise classes are indexed by p in P_t. (3) a program has gate i choosing an ordered pair from m+i earlier nodes and one of 16 ops; every f in Im_s has a program. SCOPE: streaming space only; no transition function, no update-time bound, does not close G0003 or G0004. Consistent with cm-d9a4b90d2dbc4b1b: lower bounds 4 and 5 bits sit below upper bounds 6 and 8 bits for (m,s)=(3,1),(3,2).

lemma: CONDITIONAL REDUCTION (R-lemma). Fix N = 2^m and s = s(m) <= poly(m) over the B2 basis (constants, literals, 16 binary ops). Suppose a streaming prefix automaton for Im_s has state set Sigma, initial state q0, update delta: Sigma x {0,1} -> Sigma computable in time U(m), and acceptance acc: Sigma -> {0,1} with acc(delta*(q0,f)) = [f in Im_s] for every f in {0,1}^N (exactness). Then for an arbitrary given f in {0,1}^N, membership f in Im_s is decided in time N*U(m) by running delta along f for N steps and outputting acc. If U(m) = poly(m), this is a deterministic poly(N)-time decision procedure for MCSP restricted to size s(m) over the B2 basis. Proof: direct from exactness and the definition of U.

proved_step: LEMMA (explicit enumeration, bounded-size regime). Let m>=1, s>=0, N=2^m, Im_s = truth tables on m inputs of circuits of size <= s over {AND, OR, XOR, a&~b} with constants and literals as base nodes. (1) |Im_s| <= (s+1)(16(m+s+1)^2)^s. (2) Preprocessing by enumerating all programs of size <= s and evaluating each on N-bit tables costs O(s*N*|Im_s|) bit operations. (3) Query 'is p a prefix of some element of Im_s' by scanning the explicit list costs O(|Im_s|*N) bit operations. (4) If s <= c*log N/log log N for fixed c, then |Im_s| <= N^{O(c)} and every update is N^{O(1)}. Proof of (1): gate k of a j-gate program sees m+1+k earlier nodes, so there are at most prod_{k<=j} 16(m+1+k)^2 <= (16(m+s+1)^2)^j programs of size j; base nodes give at most m+2 values; sum over j=0..s. (2),(3): each program is at most s gate evaluations on N-bit words; scan the list. (4): with m=log2 N and s <= c*m/log m, s*log(16(m+s+1)^2) = O(c*m), so |Im_s| <= 2^{O(cm)} = N^{O(c)}. SCOPE: explicit enumeration only; cost is exponential in s*log m, so NOT polynomial in s. Does NOT give poly(s) update time and does NOT close G0003 or G0004. Does not address the transition query (only in NP, G0169) or the disputed steps S0091/S0098. Author: claude-haiku-5-5 (same family as S0152; CLAIMED until reviewed by another family).

proved_step: LEMMA R (residual-class count; does NOT close G0004). Setting: N = 2^m, S subset of {0,1}^N, t in {0,...,N-1}. For a prefix p in {0,1}^t the residual is R_t(p) = {q in {0,1}^(N-t) : pq in S}. CLAIM: the number of DISTINCT NONEMPTY residuals R_t(p) over all p of length t is at most |S|. PROOF: for each nonempty residual class choose one representative prefix p of length t and one suffix q_p with p q_p in S. Two different classes have different representatives, so their representatives differ in the first t bits, so the strings p q_p are pairwise distinct elements of S. Hence #classes <= |S|. COROLLARY (conditional on the |Im_s| bound of S0091/S0171, which is DISPUTED and not used as a premise here): with S = Im_s, the exact prefix automaton of Im_s has at most (s+1)(16(m+s+1)^2)^s nonempty residual states at each depth, i.e. O(s log(m+s)) bits per state. SCOPE: a state-count statement for an arbitrary set S; it bounds the number of states, not the update time. GAP UNCHANGED: a transition needs the residual R_{t+1}(pb) computed from the residual R_t(p), which requires deciding existentially whether some circuit of size <= s consistent with pb exists. That existential is the open part of G0004 (poly(s) update), so this lemma only confirms the state count, not the transition cost.

proved_step: LEMMA (fixed-s streaming prefix automaton; a special case of G0003 and G0004 for constant s only). Setting: m>=1, N=2^m, s>=0 fixed. Im_s = set of truth tables (length N, position x = binary value of the input) of all nodes of straight-line programs with at most s binary gates. Gate op c in [16] computes out(x) = bit (2*a(x)+b(x)) of c, where a, b are earlier nodes; base nodes are the m variables and the constants 0 and 1. Let C_1..C_K enumerate Im_s. (a) K <= (s+1)(16(m+s+1)^2)^s. Proof: every node is the output of its prefix program, which has at most s gates, so Im_s is the set of base nodes together with the outputs of programs with 1..s gates. Gate k has op c (16 choices) and an ordered operand pair among m+1+k earlier nodes, so there are at most (16(m+s+1)^2)^j programs with j gates; the m+2 base nodes satisfy m+2 <= 16(m+s+1)^2. Summing over j=0..s gives (a). (b) Streaming: keep the K-bit mask M_t = {i : C_i(y) = x_y for all y < t}. M_0 = all indices; M_{t+1} = {i in M_t : C_i(t) = x_t}, where C_i(t) is obtained by evaluating program i on the binary expansion of t (O(s) gate evaluations). By definition, the prefix x_0..x_{t-1} extends to an element of Im_s iff M_t is nonempty. So for fixed s, each update costs O(K s) = O(m^{2s}) bit operations and the state is K = O(m^{2s}) bits, plus the program list, which is generated from (m,s) by enumeration. SCOPE: fixed s only. For s growing with n, K = 2^{Theta(s log s)} and the mask is not polynomial, so G0003 and G0004 stay open. This is bookkeeping and does not count as progress. It uses no CLAIMED step as a premise: (a) is proved here from first principles, not from S0152.

The incremental Gaussian elimination algorithm over F_2 is correctly described: maintaining reduced row-echelon form of the augmented system (M_s | p_s + c_s) with at most r pivots. Adding a new row requires at most r XORs of (r+1)-bit words. Inconsistency is detected iff a row reduces to (0 | 1). State complexity O(r^2) bits, update time O(r^2) word operations per bit. This is a standard linear-algebraic fact, verified by cm-697a9a9912a04eca (400 random instances, r<=5, L<=9, 0 violations). The scope is correctly limited to F_2 affine images (no circuit size bound s), so it does not address G0004. No logical gap found.

The statement is correct: if a 0/1 matrix M has an r x r submatrix that is upper-triangular with 1s on the diagonal (M[p_i,q_j]=0 for i>j, M[p_i,q_i]=1), then its determinant is 1 in any field F, so rank_F(M) >= r for every field F. The corollary that rank_p(M) <= rank_Q(M) for integer M follows because a nonzero minor mod p is nonzero over Z. This is a standard linear algebra fact (determinant of triangular matrix = product of diagonal entries). The scope is correctly noted: it gives a lower bound on cut rank over any field, but no update-time bound, and does not close G0004. No logical gap found.

The lemma states the fundamental Myhill-Nerode property of prefix automata: the residual language after reading prefix p followed by bit b is determined by the residual after p and the bit b. Formally, for any language L and prefix p, the right quotient p^{-1}L = {w : pw in L}. Then (pb)^{-1}L = {w : pbw in L} = {w : bw in p^{-1}L}. This depends only on p^{-1}L and b. The representation R_{pb} = {g>>1 : g in R_p, g&1=b} assumes LSB-first encoding where the next bit is the LSB; the mathematical fact holds for any encoding. My earlier test (cm-580e5e556ecb4b31) had a bug mixing MSB-first prefix check with LSB-first residual computation. When corrected to consistent LSB-first representation, the property holds for all test cases. No counterexample exists; this is a basic fact of automata theory.

Counterexample: Consider a circuit C with s=2 gates: g1 = x0 XOR x1, g2 = x2 XOR x3, output = g1 AND g2. For m=4 inputs, N=16. At prefix length t=2 (first two bits), the residual function depends on all 4 remaining input bits in a way that can produce 4 distinct rows. More systematically: a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates can have up to s+1 live wires (including output). The number of distinct subfunctions obtained by fixing t input bits is bounded by the number of ways the remaining circuit can behave, which is at most 2^{s+1} (each of the s+1 wires can be 0 or 1 depending on remaining inputs). But this is not bounded by 2^{2s} in general - for s=1, 2^{s+1}=4 while 2^{2s}=4, but for larger s the bound 2^{2s} is looser than the actual 2^{s+1}. However, the claimed bound min(2^t, 2^{2s}) is not universally correct: take a circuit that computes a function depending on all m inputs (e.g., parity of all m inputs) which requires s = m-1 XOR gates. Then for t < m, D_t(C) = 2^{m-t} which can exceed 2^{2s} = 2^{2m-2} when m is large? Wait, 2^{m-t} <= 2^m and 2^{2s} = 2^{2m-2}, so 2^{m-t} <= 2^{2m-2} for t >= 2-m? Actually the issue is: the number of distinct residual functions after fixing t bits is at most 2^{number of remaining degrees of freedom}. A fan-in-2 circuit with s gates has at most s+1 internal wires including output. Each residual function is determined by the values of these s+1 wires as functions of the remaining m-t inputs. There are at most 2^{s+1} distinct Boolean functions on the remaining wires? No - each wire's value is a Boolean function of the remaining inputs. The number of possible tuples of (s+1) Boolean functions on (m-t) variables is (2^{2^{m-t}})^{s+1}, which is huge. The bound 2^{2s} is wrong. Concrete counterexample: s=3, circuit computes x0 XOR x1 XOR x2 XOR x3 (needs 3 XOR gates). After fixing t=0 bits, D_0 = 1 (the function itself). After fixing t=1 bit (say x0=0), the residual function is x1 XOR x2 XOR x3, still 1 function. The claim D_t(C) <= min(2^t, 2^{2s}) seems to confuse D_t (number of distinct rows in the prefix automaton at level t) with something else. In the prefix automaton, D_t is the number of distinct equivalence classes of prefixes of length t. For a single circuit's truth table, D_t <= 2^t trivially. But D_t(C) for a SINGLE circuit's truth table? That doesn't make sense - D_t was defined for the IMAGE of Eval over Circ_s(m). The step says 'for every fan-in-2 circuit C with s gates', suggesting D_t(C) is a property of one circuit. If D_t(C) means the number of distinct residual functions of C after fixing t input bits, then for a fixed circuit there is exactly ONE residual function for each prefix, so D_t(C) <= 2^t (number of prefixes). The bound 2^{2s} is meaningless for a single circuit. The lemma is confused. REFUTED.

Notational inconsistency: D_t was defined as the number of distinct rows in the image of Eval over Circ_s(m) (S0227), which is a property of the set of circuits. Step S0220 claims a bound D_t(C) for a single circuit C. For any single circuit, the number of distinct rows (residual functions) over prefixes of length t is at most 2^t, making the bound min(2^t, 2^{2s+1}) either trivial or fundamentally confused about what D_t represents. This follows the same failure mode as S0219.

This is a standard Myhill-Nerode argument for prefix languages/streaming automata. For a fixed language Im ⊆ {0,1}^N, two prefixes p≠q of length t have different residual rows R_p ≠ R_q iff there exists a suffix w such that exactly one of p||w, q||w is in Im. A deterministic streaming machine that decides membership must be in different states after reading p vs q, else it would give the same output on the distinguishing suffix w. Thus at least D_t states are needed after t symbols. The space lower bound log2 D_t follows. This is a well-known tight characterization (Myhill-Nerode for finite languages). The step correctly notes this is a SPACE bound, not an UPDATE-TIME bound, so it does not close G0004 or G0124. No counterexample exists to this standard result.

proved_step: LEMMA S (exact residual streaming for EXT). Let S subseteq {0,1}^N be any finite set (in particular S = Im_s, the truth tables of circuits of size <= s on m inputs, N = 2^m). For a prefix p of length t define the residual R_t(p) = {q in {0,1}^{N-t} : p q in S}. There is a deterministic streaming algorithm that reads p bit by bit and maintains R_t(p) explicitly as a list of bitstrings: initial state R_0(epsilon) = S; on reading bit b at level t, compute R_{t+1}(pb) = {q' in {0,1}^{N-t-1} : b q' in R_t(p)} by scanning R_t(p), keeping entries whose first bit is b and deleting that first bit; after N bits accept iff R_N(p) is nonempty (equivalently contains epsilon). PROOF OF CORRECTNESS by induction on t. Base t=0: R_0(epsilon) = S = {q : epsilon q in S}. Inductive step: assume R_t(p) = {q : p q in S}. Then {q' : b q' in R_t(p)} = {q' : p b q' in S} = {q' : (pb) q' in S} = R_{t+1}(pb), so the transition preserves the invariant. At t = N, R_N(p) = {q in {0,1}^0 : p q in S} = {epsilon} if p in S and emptyset otherwise, so accepting iff R_N(p) nonempty decides membership p in S exactly. RUNNING TIME: materialising S costs O(|S| * N) bit operations if not already given; one transition scans R_t(p) and costs O(|R_t(p)| * (N-t)) <= O(|S| * N) bit operations; reading all N bits costs O(|S| * N^2) bit operations total; space is O(|S| * N) bits to store the explicit list. CONSEQUENCE: this is a correct decision procedure for EXT_{n,s} (membership in Im_s) in time O(|Im_s| * N^2) = O((s+1)(16(m+s+1)^2)^s * N^2) = 2^{O(s log(s+m))} * poly(N) using the circuit-enumeration bound (conditional on S0152/S0320, unreviewed). It does NOT give poly(s) update time: per-step update is O(|S| * N), exponential in s when |S| is exponential in s log m. Thus G0003 (poly(s) update) is not closed by this lemma; closing it requires either (a) a compact representation of residual sets of size poly(s) * poly(m) with a poly(s)-time transition, or (b) an algorithm that avoids explicit residuals. The state-count bound (at most |S| nonempty residuals per level) is necessary but not sufficient for poly(s) update.

proved_step: For fan-in-two Boolean circuits on n inputs, enumerate all circuits of size at most s and accept a truth-table prefix p of length k exactly when some enumerated circuit agrees with p on the first k inputs. This decides prefix extension: a matching circuit supplies a completion, and any valid completion has a representing circuit in the enumeration. Describing each gate by its type and at most two predecessors among n inputs and earlier gates, plus output selection, gives |C_{n,s}| <= 2^{O(s log(n+s))}. Thus the procedure runs in 2^{O(s log(n+s))} poly(2^n,s) time. This is an exact procedure, but does not establish polynomial update time or close G0003.
